explanation: Build a shared prefix trie for all dictionary words, then backtrack over board paths while following trie edges. A terminal marker stores a complete word; remove it after reporting that word to suppress duplicates. Delete exhausted trie branches so later starts avoid prefixes with no unreported words.
timeComplexity: O(S + RC·4^L) upper bound for total dictionary characters S and maximum word length L: trie construction reads S characters, then each of RC board starts explores at most four choices per depth while following shared prefixes. Pruning can reduce this work.
spaceComplexity: O(S + min(L,RC)) auxiliary space: trie nodes are bounded by total dictionary characters and the used set/recursion contain only the active no-reuse path. Returned word references are output space.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: At every search call the board path spells the trie prefix and used contains exactly its cells. Following an existing edge to an unused orthogonal cell preserves that correspondence. A terminal proves a complete dictionary word; deleting only its marker preserves longer words sharing that prefix. A child with no terminal or edges has no unreported descendant, so pruning it cannot remove a future answer. Trying all starts therefore reports every realizable word exactly once.
walkthrough: For board ["ab","cd"] and words ["ab","ac","ad","bd","cab"], the trie root has a,b,c branches. Starting at a finds terminals ab and ac; ad cannot be reached orthogonally. Starting at b finds bd. Starting at c follows c→a→b to find cab. Removing each found terminal prevents repeat reporting. Return ["ab","ac","bd","cab"] in any order.
edgeCases: Words may share board cells across different searches.
One word’s path cannot reuse a cell.
Repeated dictionary entries produce one returned word.
Only horizontal and vertical moves are allowed.
